claims.text: The WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% each of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
The combination of refractory elements in WTaTiVZr governs its plastic strain and toughness under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service.
Relative to pure tungsten, the refractory-element combination in WTaTiVZr alters dislocation dynamics.
Relative to pure tungsten, the refractory-element combination in WTaTiVZr alters grain-boundary structure.
Interactions among the refractory elements produce the altered dislocation dynamics and grain-boundary structure.
The altered dislocation dynamics and grain-boundary structure enhance the alloy's ability to accommodate plastic strain.
The altered dislocation dynamics and grain-boundary structure improve the alloy's toughness relative to pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten under temperatures above 1000°C with plasma irradiation.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater toughness than pure tungsten under temperatures above 1000°C with plasma irradiation.
The hypothesis is bounded to temperatures above 1000°C in a plasma-radiation environment and may not apply at lower temperatures or without irradiation.
A controlled comparison will test as-fabricated WTaTiVZr against as-fabricated pure tungsten under the same high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
The comparison will measure plastic strain, toughness, dislocation dynamics, and grain-boundary structure.
Lower plastic strain and toughness in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten under the stated conditions would falsify or fail to support the hypothesis.
